text:
maria: Quick sync — I'm drafting a short playbook for canary telemetry + dashboarding. want to capture what metrics we show by default and what lives behind a drilldown :spiral_note_pad:

trent: +1. baseline vs canary deltas are the most important. propose: latency p50/p95, error-rate, token-cost-per-request, model-fallback-rate. show relative delta and absolute values.

lena: UX note: users need an at-a-glance 'rollback risk' indicator on the rollout card. not just numbers — a single traffic-light with tooltip explaining the driver.

maria: agree. also we should pick a canonical time window. 5m for realtime, 1h for stability. which do we default to in the console?

trent: default to 1h with a fast toggle to 5m. 1h smooths noisy token-cost and cold-start blips.

kai: internal-api question — are we exposing "/rollouts/{id}/telemetry" that returns precomputed deltas, or do we let frontend query raw series and compute deltas client-side?

lena: we prefer server-side deltas for consistent alerting and smaller payloads. client-side computation leads to drift between alerts and UI view.

ashley: server-side deltas also let us attach reasons to guards (e.g., "p95 > baseline by 20% due to model change"). but it's heavier on compute. need to think cost/quotas.

maria: thinking: precompute deltas in a materialized view every 1m, store recent 24h. keep raw series available for adhoc drilldowns beyond 24h.

opsbot: deploy scheduled: rollout/8902 -> canary (10% traffic) started by @maria at 1909876600.

deploy-bot: canary healthcheck: all pods live, routes up, 200 OK on /health.

canary-bot: synthetic run #23: p95=380ms (+18% vs baseline), errors=0.5% (+0.3pp).

trent: the +18% p95 is within expected? i'd say >15% should raise a caution guard. propose guard thresholds be configurable per product.

lena: UI behavior: when a guard trips show a non-modal banner on the rollout page + an option to pause traffic with one click. also add 'why' drilldown to surface contributing slices (region/model/route).

kai: API naming bikeshed: /rollouts/{id}/signals vs /rollouts/{id}/telemetry. signals aligns with alerting, telemetry feels raw. leaning toward /signals for precomputed guards.

maria: +1 to /signals for computed deltas and guard reasons, /metrics for raw series. keep both.

ashley: question about alerting: do we send alerts from the platform alerting service or let users wire their own PagerDuty? we should send platform-level critical alerts and provide a webhook for customers.

trent: platform alerts only for severity=critical (e.g., rollout causing increased 5xxs). everything else is user-configurable and emitted as events to their webhooks.

maria: storage retention tradeoff: keep 1m precomputed deltas for 24h, 5m aggregated deltas for 30d, and raw metrics downsampled for 90d. that keeps costs reasonable.

lena: drilldown UX: when clicking a metric delta, show a waterfall of contributing dimensions and a small table of top 5 impacted routes. allow 'open in metrics' for full exploration.

kai: implementation note: backend will publish both a compact signals protobuf and an expanded JSON. UI reads signals JSON; alerting uses protobuf API for efficiency.

maria: example guard payload (draft):
```json
{
  "guard_id": "p95-regression-1",
  "threshold": 0.15,
  "window": "60m",
  "metric": "latency_p95",
  "mode": "automatic-pause",
  "explanation": "p95 +18% vs baseline"
}
```

ashley: make sure quotas are enforced on telemetry query endpoints; customers on free tier get 1m resolution and limited history. dedicated customers get higher retention and faster compute windows.

trent: also add a conditional route fallback policy: if model fallback-rate > X AND errors increasing, route to cheaper baseline model. this reduces user impact.

maria: action items: 1) kai protos for /signals + /metrics schema 2) trent + ashley define default guard thresholds per metric 3) lena wireframe 'rollback risk' and drilldown 4) ops: add platform alert mapping for sev-critical.

lena: i'll mock the banner and single-click pause in Figma today, ping @maria when done. :paintbrush:

kai: i'll draft the API routes and a sample protobuf by EOD tomorrow.

opsbot: note: please file infra ticket for materialized-view compute pad to avoid noisy billing spikes.

maria: thanks all. this playbook will live under /docs/rollouts/canary-telemetry-playbook.md once we have prototypes. feel free to drop quick thoughts below. :rocket:
